content: 1. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of axitinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction is relevant only for the oral forms of both drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. 2. Blessed thistle diminishes the effects of famotidine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is theoretical, and its clinical significance is unknown. 3. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of ceftibuten by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 4. Famotidine reduces cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction is relevant only for oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 5. Devil's claw reduces the effects of famotidine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 6. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of famotidine through an unspecified mechanism. Isavuconazonium sulfate, an OCT2 inhibitor, may enhance the effects or levels of OCT2 substrates. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 7. Famotidine increases metformin levels by reducing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Famotidine decreases the levels of phytoestrogens by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents, and its clinical significance is unknown. 9. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by increasing gastric pH. Acalabrutinib solubility decreases as gastric pH increases. Administer acalabrutinib at least 2 hours before an H2-receptor antagonist. Monitor therapy closely. 10. Famotidine increases alendronate levels through an unspecified mechanism. Monitor for increased side effects of alendronate. 11. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of aripiprazole through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of atazanavir by increasing gastric pH. Atazanavir solubility decreases as pH increases, leading to substantially reduced plasma concentrations. For treatment-naïve patients, administer atazanavir simultaneously with the H2-receptor antagonist or at least 10 hours afterward. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of bosutinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Famotidine reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent, and coadministration with drugs that increase gastric pH may cause premature dissolution, potentially affecting drug release and absorption in the duodenum. Monitor therapy closely. 15. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of carbonyl iron by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 16. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of cefdinir, cefditoren, cefpodoxime, ceftibuten, and cefuroxime by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 17. Famotidine decreases crizotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Drugs that elevate gastric pH may reduce crizotinib solubility and bioavailability. No formal studies have been conducted. Use caution and monitor therapy. 18. Famotidine increases cyclosporine levels through an unknown mechanism. Delayed absorption of cyclosporine has been reported when coadministered with famotidine. Use caution and monitor therapy. 19. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of dabrafenib by increasing gastric pH. Drugs that alter upper gastrointestinal tract pH (e.g., PPIs, H2-blockers, antacids) may decrease dabrafenib solubility and bioavailability. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of dapsone by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of dasatinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Famotidine increases the levels or effects of dexmethylphenidate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to extended-release formulations. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 23. Famotidine increases digoxin levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Famotidine increases erdafitinib levels by reducing renal clearance. Consider alternatives that are not OCT2 substrates or reduce the dose of OCT2 substrates based on tolerability. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 25. Famotidine decreases erlotinib levels through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid combination when possible. If concurrent use is required, administer erlotinib 10 hours after an H2-antagonist and at least 2 hours before the next dose of the H2-antagonist. Use caution and monitor therapy. 26. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, ferrous sulfate, and iron dextran complex by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 27. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 28. Famotidine reduces gefitinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Separate gefitinib and H2-antagonist doses by at least 6 hours. Use caution and monitor therapy. 29. Famotidine increases glipizide and glyburide levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 30. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 31. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. If use with an acid-reducing agent cannot be avoided, administer infigratinib 2 hours before or 10 hours after an H2-antagonist. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of mesalamine by increasing gastric pH. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Famotidine increases methylphenidate levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to extended-release formulations. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 34. Famotidine and mifepristone may increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor therapy. 35. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 36. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of nelfinavir by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 37. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of neratinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Famotidine reduces nilotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid this interaction by administering H2-antagonists 10 hours after or 2 hours before nilotinib. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 39. Famotidine decreases the levels or effects of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration with drugs that raise gastric pH. Consider short-acting antacids instead of PPIs and H2-antagonists, and separate antacid and pazopanib dosing by several hours. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Famotidine increases pexidartinib levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate pexidartinib by 2 hours before or 10 hours after taking an H2-antagonist. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Famotidine decreases the levels of phytoestrogens by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 42. Famotidine and pimozide may increase each other's toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 44. Famotidine decreases ponatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Famotidine reduces the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 46. Pretomanid increases famotidine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Pretomanid significantly inhibits OAT3 in vitro. Monitor for increased adverse effects and consider dosage reduction for OAT3 substrates. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Famotidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Concurrent use may cause treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. Administer H2-antagonists at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 48. Famotidine increases risedronate levels by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
